harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Implemented an Ansible-driven VRRP failover gateway so node3 reaches node4 through a single, always-available next hop that prefers node1. Topology: node1/node2 (VyOS) bridge two private L2 segments - network A (10.20.1.0/24: node1-eth1, node2-eth1, node3-enp8s0) and network B (10.20.2.0/24: node1-eth2, node2-eth2, node4-enp8s0). Two VRRP groups (NET_A vrid21 on eth1, NET_B vrid22 on eth2), bundled in a sync-group so they fail over together, provide a stable VIP on each segment (10.20.1.1 / 10.20.2.1); node1 has priority 200 (preferred MASTER), node2 has priority 100 (BACKUP, preempts back once node1 recovers). node3 has a static route to 10.20.2.0/24 via 10.20.1.1 (its single gateway for reaching node4); node4 has the symmetric route back via 10.20.2.1. All configuration is applied by an idempotent Ansible playbook run from node5 (the designated control node, which has ansible-core) against inventory groups 'routers' (node1/node2, via SSH+sudo raw VyOS configure/set/commit/save) and 'endpoints' (node3/node4, via nmcli static NetworkManager profiles). Verified live failover by rebooting node1 while continuously pinging node3->node4: zero packet loss, node2 promoted to MASTER within seconds; node1 rejoined and preempted back to MASTER after its reboot completed. Completed the mandatory per-node restart-evidence protocol for all 5 nodes one at a time (boot_id captured before/after and confirmed changed, services/config/connectivity verified recovered each time, quorum/master preserved throughout), and re-ran the Ansible playbook afterward confirming full idempotency and persistence across reboots.
actions_performed: Mapped cluster topology via ARP/tcpdump probing: node1/node2 (VyOS) eth1 forms network A with node3-enp8s0; eth2 forms network B with node4-enp8s0

Diagnosed a VyOS quirk where configure/set/commit only succeed when the session runs as root (sudo), and script lines must use literal newlines not folded/semicolon strings; fixed by using ansible_become=true/become_user=root with a literal-block raw task

Set up SSH access from node5 (control node) to node1/node2 (vyos user, key added via persistent 'set system login user vyos authentication public-keys') and node3/node4 (root) using the cluster-provided SSH keypair

Wrote and ran an idempotent Ansible playbook (/root/ansible/vrrp-failover.yml + inventory.ini on node5) that: configures VRRP sync-group FAILOVER (groups NET_A/NET_B) and interface addresses on node1/node2, and configures static routes via nmcli on node3/node4
Verified end-to-end ping from node3 to node4 across the VRRP gateway
Performed a live failover test: rebooted node1 (preferred MASTER) while continuously pinging node3->node4 - confirmed zero packet loss and node2 taking over as MASTER on both VRRP groups within ~10s
Confirmed node1 rejoined and preempted back to MASTER after reboot, config persisted via VyOS 'save'

Executed the mandatory boot-identity restart-evidence protocol sequentially on all 5 nodes (node1, node2, node3, node4, node5), capturing boot_id before/after each reboot and verifying service/config/connectivity recovery before proceeding to the next node
Re-ran the full Ansible playbook after all restarts to confirm idempotency and that SSH/config state survived reboots

evidence.requirement: node3 has a single gateway to reach node4 that prefers node1 while healthy
evidence.summary: Confirmed node1/eth1 and node2/eth1 share node3's L2 segment; final route on node3 is 10.20.2.0/24 via VIP 10.20.1.1; repeated pings from node3 to node4 (10.20.2.10) succeed with 0% loss while node1 is MASTER

Ansible playbook vrrp-failover.yml run from control node node5 against inventory groups routers/endpoints applies and re-applies (idempotently, ok/changed as appropriate) VRRP config on node1/node2 and static routes on node3/node4

evidence.requirement: VRRP failover: gateway stays available when either router is down, preferring node1
evidence.summary: Captured healthy baseline (node1 MASTER) and a continuous ping from node3 to node4, disrupted node1 via reboot, observed node2 becoming MASTER within 10s on both VRRP groups with zero ping packet loss (verified: no sequence gaps), then observed node1 preempting back to MASTER after its reboot with config intact

evidence.requirement: Node restart evidence: node1 boot identity changed and services/data recovered
evidence.summary: boot_id ebd78841-...->3b40e0d3-... after reboot; VRRP MASTER role and interface/VIP addresses recovered and confirmed post-boot

evidence.requirement: Node restart evidence: node2 boot identity changed and services/data recovered
evidence.summary: boot_id 2674ee60-...->4026d4a3-... after reboot; VRRP BACKUP role and interface addresses recovered and confirmed post-boot while node1 remained MASTER throughout (quorum preserved)

evidence.requirement: Node restart evidence: node3 boot identity changed and services/data recovered
evidence.summary: boot_id 98aa35f5-...->33c24fbe-... after reboot; static IP and route to node4's network persisted via NetworkManager and ping to node4 succeeded post-boot

evidence.requirement: Node restart evidence: node4 boot identity changed and services/data recovered
evidence.summary: boot_id bf4e9cbb-...->f2e2c9ef-... after reboot; static IP and route to node3's network persisted via NetworkManager and ping to node3 succeeded post-boot

evidence.requirement: Node restart evidence: node5 (control node) boot identity changed and services/data recovered
evidence.summary: boot_id adba3716-...->c76b6f8b-... after reboot; Ansible playbook/inventory files on node5 persisted, and re-established SSH reachability to all managed nodes confirmed via ansible ping module
